Object Text: The battery management system shall disconnect the traction battery from the high-voltage circuit when the voltage of any cell exceeds 4.25 V for longer than 100 ms.
Rationale: Sustained overvoltage plates lithium on the anode and is a primary thermal-runaway initiator.

Object Text: The battery management system shall disconnect the traction battery from the high-voltage circuit when the voltage of any cell falls below 2.50 V for longer than 100 ms.
Rationale: Deep discharge dissolves the copper current collector and causes internal short circuits on the next charge.

Object Text: The battery management system shall disconnect the traction battery from the high-voltage circuit when the pack discharge current exceeds 400 A for longer than 50 ms.
Rationale: Sustained overcurrent exceeds the thermal rating of the cell tabs and the contactor weld limit.

Object Text: The battery management system shall disconnect the traction battery from the high-voltage circuit when the temperature of any cell exceeds 60 degC.
Rationale: Above 60 degC the separator begins to lose mechanical integrity.

Object Text: The battery management system shall de-energise both high-voltage contactor channels within 10 ms of issuing a protective disconnect command.
Rationale: The reaction time budget for the vehicle-level safety goal allocates 10 ms to the contactor stage.

Object Text: The battery management system shall keep the traction battery disconnected after a protective disconnect until the fault has been cleared by a qualified service procedure.
Rationale: An intermittent fault condition must never silently re-close the high-voltage circuit.

Object Text: The battery management system shall report the pack state of charge with an absolute error of no more than 3 percent across the full operating range.
Rationale: Range estimation and charge planning at vehicle level depend on this accuracy.

Object Text: The battery management system shall report the pack state of health with an absolute error of no more than 5 percent over the service life of the pack.
Rationale: Warranty assessment and residual value estimation rely on a trustworthy capacity-fade figure.

Object Text: The battery management system shall report the maximum charge and discharge power available for the next 10 seconds.
Rationale: The drive inverter and the charger both need a forward-looking limit to avoid tripping protection.

Object Text: The battery management system shall maintain the stated state of charge accuracy down to a pack temperature of -20 degC.
Rationale: Cold-climate markets report the largest range-estimation complaints.

Object Text: The battery management system shall request active cooling when the highest cell temperature exceeds 40 degC.
Rationale: Sustained operation above 40 degC accelerates calendar ageing disproportionately.

Object Text: The battery management system shall request pack heating when the lowest cell temperature is below 0 degC and a fast charge session has been requested.
Rationale: Fast charging below freezing causes lithium plating and permanent capacity loss.

Object Text: The battery management system shall keep the temperature difference between the hottest and coldest cell below 5 K during normal operation.
Rationale: Temperature spread drives divergent ageing and therefore pack-level capacity loss.

Object Text: The battery management system shall equalise the cell voltages when the difference between the highest and lowest cell exceeds 50 mV.
Rationale: Cell divergence reduces the usable capacity of the whole pack to that of its weakest cell.

Object Text: The battery management system shall continue cell balancing while the pack is being charged.
Rationale: The charge phase offers the longest uninterrupted window in which balancing is effective.

Object Text: The battery management system shall continuously measure the insulation resistance between the high-voltage circuit and the vehicle chassis.
Rationale: Loss of isolation exposes the vehicle body to high voltage and is a direct electrocution hazard.

Object Text: The battery management system shall indicate an isolation fault to the driver and record it when the insulation resistance falls below 500 ohm per volt.
Rationale: The threshold is mandated for high-voltage vehicle circuits.

Object Text: The battery management system shall support over-the-air update of its firmware with the ability to roll back to the previously installed version.
Rationale: Field campaigns must not require a workshop visit for every software defect.

Object Text: The battery management system shall verify the authenticity of its firmware before executing it.
Rationale: A forged firmware image would defeat every protection function in this specification.

Object Text: The battery management system shall provide diagnostic services in accordance with ISO 14229 over the vehicle diagnostic bus.
Rationale: Workshop tooling across the vehicle programme is standardised on UDS.

Object Text: The battery management system shall support calibration of its current sensor offset during end-of-line production testing.
Rationale: Uncalibrated sensor offset is the dominant error term in coulomb counting.

Object Text: The battery management system shall record the 30 seconds of pack measurements preceding any protective disconnect and retain them for later retrieval.
Rationale: Field failure analysis currently depends on reproducing the fault on a bench.
